snapshot.command: RPC_MAINNET=$RPC_MAINNET node scripts/snapshot-depletion-stakers.js && RPC_MAINNET=$RPC_MAINNET node scripts/snapshot-phlimbo-v2-stakers.js
snapshot.intentComment: PREREQUISITE for :dry / :broadcast / :resume. Story 076 ADDED A SECOND SNAPSHOT to this key, joined with '&&' so a failure in either halts the chain: scripts/snapshot-phlimbo-v2-stakers.js writes scripts/snapshots/phlimbo-v2-snapshot-latest.json, which Phase 4e seeds MigratorV2V3 from. Unlike the depletion-staker snapshot it is an ADDRESS LIST ONLY -- MigratorV2V3 reads every position live off V2 (MigratorV2V3.sol:20-24), so no amount is seeded and none could be trusted if it were. It must NOT be taken after a pause: PhlimboV2 is deliberately never paused for this migration.

dry.command: node scripts/check-phlimbo-snapshot-age.js --variant v2 --fail-on-stale && PREVIEW_MODE=true forge script script/DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol:DeployMainnetPromotionReady --rpc-url $RPC_MAINNET --slow -vvv
dry.intentComment: Dry run against LIVE mainnet state: impersonates the owner, signs nothing, broadcasts nothing, writes NO progress file (a preview CREATE address is fork-local fiction and would poison the patcher). Runs Phase 0's structural preconditions and Phase 7's full bidirectional wiring read-back, then Phase 8's preview-only smoke tests: the BLOCKING Kendu fee-on-transfer probe (round-trips a real amount through collectNudge and asserts the credited buffer delta equals the amount sent - if Kendu is taxed it must NOT be whitelisted and its mainnet-addresses.ts key stays a zero placeholder), MintPageView.getData() resolution, a donation on each dispatcher donor path with the pooler verified POSITIVELY via BatchDonatedViaPSM (its _psmDonate failures are swallowed by a try/catch, so a green transaction proves nothing), a qualifying 40-mint batchMint after a vm.warp so the streamed pot has accrued, the BatchMint__ArrayLengthMismatch negative test (which sits OUTSIDE any broadcast/prank block - a reverting call inside a broadcast block is queued as a real transaction and aborts the run), and the BPT recovery path. This dry run is the verification gate for story 072. STORY 076: the dry run is also where Phase 4e is proved. Phase 0 now validates the V2 staker snapshot (target address, block number, and age against MAX_V2_SNAPSHOT_AGE) and records the write-once baselines.phlimboV2StakedAtCutover; the migration itself runs under the owner prank, so the decoded UserMigrationSkipped reasons and the totalStaked()==0 completeness gate are exercised HERE, before any Ledger session -- which is exactly where a straggler or a dust position should first surface. Phase 8 adds two probes: a PhlimboV3 stake -> warp 30d -> claim round trip asserting the phUSD reward leg ACTUALLY PAYS (wallet balance up AND unclaimablePhUSDOf still zero -- checking only the first would pass on a claim that banked everything), and the cheap SolvencyDetermination.md section-1 principal invariant phUSD.balanceOf(phlimboV3) >= totalStaked. The V2-snapshot staleness gate (check-phlimbo-snapshot-age.js --variant v2 --fail-on-stale, 24h) is PREPENDED to :dry, :broadcast and :resume alike. It is --fail-on-stale rather than the V1 key's --auto-refresh on purpose: a silent regeneration would move the seed list out from under an operator who is comparing a dry run against the broadcast they are about to sign. Re-run promotion-ready:snapshot explicitly. Phase 0 independently re-checks the age on-chain against block.timestamp, so the gate cannot be bypassed by editing the file's ISO timestamp alone.

broadcast.command: node scripts/check-phlimbo-snapshot-age.js --variant v2 --fail-on-stale && node scripts/backup-mainnet-addresses.js && forge script script/DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol:DeployMainnetPromotionReady --rpc-url $RPC_MAINNET --broadcast --skip-simulation --slow --ledger --hd-paths "m/44'/60'/46'/0/0" --legacy --with-gas-price 0.5gwei --gas-estimate-multiplier 200 -vvv && node scripts/patch-mainnet-addresses-promotion-ready.js && npm run promotion-ready:verify

post: npm run promotion-ready:verify  (-> forge script VerifyPromotionReady, read-only)

broadcast.skipSimulationNote: --skip-simulation removes only the pre-send sanity check, NOT forge's single LOCAL execution pass. The whole cutover body (Phase 0, every in-phase post-condition, all of Phase 7) still evaluates ONCE against PRE-broadcast state before transaction #1 is dispatched. This is the 'ForgeLocalPassPrecedesBroadcast' property established in audit run-23; it is why the trailing verify leg exists and why in-body assertions prove plan self-consistency, never chain outcome.
broadcast.chainOrderingRule: The '&& node scripts/patch-mainnet-addresses-promotion-ready.js' leg is MANDATORY and MUST BE THE FINAL STATE-MUTATING ELEMENT; it is followed only by the read-only '&& npm run promotion-ready:verify' and by nothing else. '&&' not ';' — it must run ONLY on a zero exit from forge script.
broadcast.intentComment: LIVE BROADCAST. --legacy plus a small flat --with-gas-price is the story-071 lesson: forge's EIP-1559 maxFeePerGas dips below base fee during a long --slow Ledger session and geth rejects the tx at eth_sendRawTransaction. Legacy type-0 txes have no maxFeePerGas field so that rule cannot fire - but with --legacy the gas price is the FLAT PRICE PAID, so keep it a small multiple of base fee (~0.5 gwei), never 2 gwei+ (that overpaid ~13x on the cutover). --gas-estimate-multiplier 200 is story 073's lesson: under --slow each transaction is a new block, so timestamp-dependent accrual (_updatePool, depositFor) does real SSTORE work the single-timestamp simulation pass never sees; 073 hit OutOfGas on the second depositFor with forge's default 130% headroom. On mainnet this raises the gas LIMIT, not the price paid - with --legacy --with-gas-price unused gas is refunded, so the cost is bounded. THE TRAILING '&& node scripts/patch-mainnet-addresses-promotion-ready.js' IS MANDATORY AND MUST BE THE FINAL STATE-MUTATING ELEMENT OF THE CHAIN - it is followed by the read-only 'npm run promotion-ready:verify' leg (story 075) and by nothing else; never insert anything that writes between them. It is not an optional convenience: the broadcast is not complete until mainnet-addresses.ts reflects the new lineup. '&&' not ';' - it must run ONLY on a zero exit from forge script, because patching from a failed or partial broadcast writes addresses for contracts that may not exist. It is preceded by backup-mainnet-addresses.js so the pre-cutover file is recoverable. It FILLS the NudgeStreamer and Kendu zero placeholders and REPOINTS every update:true key, adds and removes NO keys (the key-set equality check is the tsc --strict drift guard, re-verified after patching; 55 keys as of story 078), and exits non-zero on any collision or unfilled key. THE CHAIN THEN ENDS WITH '&& npm run promotion-ready:verify' (story 075, script-audit run-22 M-01). Read that key's own doc entry before deciding it is optional: forge script executes the whole cutover body ONCE, LOCALLY, and dispatches afterwards, so Phase 0, every in-phase post-condition and all of Phase 7 had already evaluated against PRE-broadcast state before transaction #1 left the machine, and Phase 8's blocking probes are gated off entirely under broadcast. Without the verify leg the broadcast path carries NO outcome verification of any kind - the assertions prove the plan is self-consistent, never that the chain matches it. STORY 076: Phase 4e runs inside this same broadcast, between Phase 4c and Phase 5. It adds ~10-15 transactions plus one migrate() call per MIGRATE_CHUNK (25) users, each of which needs a Ledger signature -- budget the session accordingly. The mandatory patch tail is unchanged and still the final state-mutating element, followed only by the read-only verify leg; the patcher now also FILLS the PhlimboV3 zero placeholder and still never repoints PhlimboEA, which remains the V2 address. STORY 078: Phase 4f runs inside this same broadcast, immediately after Phase 4e and before Phase 5 -- two more transactions (deploy DepositPageViewV3, ViewRouter.setPage('deposit')), both Ledger-signed. The key-set is now 55, not 58: story 078 DELETED the DepositView, DepositPageView and MintPageView keys from addresses.ts and mainnet-addresses.ts in lockstep, leaving ViewRouter as the sole view key (55 == 55 is still the tsc --strict drift guard, re-verified after patching). DepositPageViewV3 is deliberately given NO key and NO FIELDS entry: ViewRouter.pages(keccak256('deposit')) publishes its address on-chain and progress.promotion-ready.1.json records it, so a hand-maintained key would only recreate the dual-resolution ambiguity that let the deposit page sit on a V1 view for months. This BREAKS downstream UI consumers that copied the ContractAddresses interface -- owner-sanctioned and adapted separately.

divergesFromBroadcast.omissionRationale: "This key OMITS the leading address backup (already taken by the crashed :broadcast run)" — verbatim from the doc key.
divergesFromBroadcast.observation: Because the backup is skipped, a :resume leg that is run WITHOUT a prior :broadcast in the same operational session (e.g. the operator's first invocation after hand-trimming a progress file) patches mainnet-addresses.ts with no fresh pre-image. The doc key asserts the backup exists rather than checking it; nothing in the chain verifies a mainnet.backup.*.ts was taken. Recorded as an observation, not a judgement.

resume.intentComment: Resumes promotion-ready:broadcast after a mid-broadcast crash. PREREQUISITE, and it is not optional: the progress file server/deployments/progress.promotion-ready.1.json is written during forge's LOCAL execution pass, BEFORE broadcasting, so after a crash IT LIES - it can name contracts that were never deployed and mark steps that never landed. Trim it by hand to only the on-chain-CONFIRMED steps (source of truth: the broadcast's run-latest.json receipts[] plus `cast nonce`), set deploymentStatus back to 'in_progress', then verify with promotion-ready:dry before re-broadcasting. THE TRIM APPLIES TO THE 'contracts' BLOCK ONLY - NEVER DELETE OR EDIT THE TOP-LEVEL 'baselines' BLOCK. 'IT LIES' is a statement about WRITE-side entries: those are recorded during forge's LOCAL pass for actions that may never have been broadcast. baselines.bptAtCutover is the opposite - a READ of pre-existing chain state taken at Phase 0 before this session dispatched anything, so no crash can falsify it, and it is the only surviving record of how much BPT the old pooler held once _moveBPT has emptied it. Preserve it verbatim (decimal string, all digits) across every trim; if pooler_bpt is marked configured and the baseline is missing, Phase 0 now ABORTS rather than silently re-deriving 0 and reducing the Phase 7 conservation assertion to 'balanceOf(newPooler) >= 0'. The deploy script is idempotent per step and its Phase 0 slot assertions are resume-aware (each index may hold either its pre-cutover dispatcher or the replacement named by the progress file). THE BPT MOVE IS THE ONE STEP A BAD RESUME COULD RUIN: it aborts outright if the old pooler's BPT balance is already 0, rather than re-running and stranding 16,338 BPT on a first, orphaned pooler. This key OMITS the leading address backup (already taken by the crashed :broadcast run) and carries the SAME mandatory patch tail, which must run after EVERY resume leg. STORY 076: the trim rule now protects THREE baselines, not one -- bptAtCutover, phusdMinterMask/phusdMintVersion, and phlimboV2StakedAtCutover. NEVER DELETE OR EDIT THE TOP-LEVEL 'baselines' BLOCK. phlimboV2StakedAtCutover is the same category of thing as bptAtCutover: a READ of pre-existing chain state taken at Phase 0 before this session dispatched anything, and the ONLY surviving record of how much stake PhlimboV2 held once the migration has emptied it. If p4e_migrate is marked configured and that baseline is missing, Phase 0 ABORTS rather than re-deriving 0 and reducing the Phase 7 conservation assertion to 'phlimboV3.totalStaked() >= 0'. Every Phase 4e step is _isConfigured-gated and idempotent; the migration pass itself is safe to re-run because MigratorV2V3 reads positions live and skips anyone already at zero.
resume.deltaNote: The :resume doc key was NOT updated by story 078. It documents the three protected baselines and every Phase 4e step, but says nothing about Phase 4f's two _isConfigured-gated steps (DepositPageViewV3 deployment record + viewRouter_setPage_deposit flag) or their trim semantics. The mechanism is present in code (both gated, both in _allProgressKeys); only the operator-facing trim documentation is silent.

verify.intentComment: READ-ONLY POST-BROADCAST VERIFICATION (story 075, script-audit run-22 M-01). No --broadcast, no --ledger, nothing signed, nothing written. Runs as a SEPARATE forge script invocation AFTER the cutover has settled, which is the entire point: forge script executes the whole cutover body once LOCALLY and dispatches the ~60 transactions afterwards, so Phase 0, every in-phase post-condition and all of _phase7_wiringAssertions() had already evaluated against PRE-broadcast state before transaction #1 left the machine, and --skip-simulation removes the pre-send sanity check rather than that local pass. Phase 8's BLOCKING probes are gated off under broadcast. This leg re-runs Phase 7's ABSOLUTE wiring assertions against LIVE chain state, plus the phUSD mint-authority invariance check that existed on no path before story 075. It CONSUMES the write-once baselines.bptAtCutover persisted by story 074 and NEVER re-derives it: post-broadcast the old pooler is always empty, so a live read yields 0 and the BPT conservation assertion would collapse to 'balanceOf(newPooler) >= 0' - the audit is explicit that a standalone verifier without the persisted baseline ACTIVELY WORSENS finding L-02 from Low to Medium. An absent or zero baseline therefore ABORTS rather than falling back. Every check is a require, so any failure exits non-zero and halts the '&&' chain. Safe to re-run at will. NOT DISCHARGED HERE and still a human step: story-072 checklist line 1197 (trigger one index-4 mint, assert BatchDonatedViaPSM fired) - it needs a real mint and cannot be done read-only. STORY 076 RESTATED ITS MINT-AUTHORITY CLAIM. Story 075 asserted INVARIANCE -- byte-identical minter-set membership -- because story 072 made zero phUSD.setMinter calls. Phase 4e makes two, so invariance would now FAIL on a correct cutover. It is replaced by an EXPECTED TWO-SIDED DELTA (the candidate mask must have lost exactly the PhlimboV2 bit and nothing else moved, with phUSD's global mintVersion still unchanged -- setMinter does not touch it, only revokeAllMintPrivileges does) plus a POSITIVE assertion that PhlimboV3 holds mint authority. PhlimboV3 is the ONE exclusion from the 'no newly deployed contract may hold mint authority' sweep; MigratorV2V3 stays in it (V2 itself mints during withdraw, so the migrator needs no role). This leg also consumes a SECOND write-once baseline, phlimboV2StakedAtCutover, and aborts if it is absent or zero -- post-broadcast PhlimboV2 is always empty by construction, so a live re-read would collapse the stake-conservation assertion to 'totalStaked >= 0' exactly as it would for the BPT position.
